name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Usability pass on the config page, driven by a failure that actually happened on this deployment: a remote server had been switched off, and nothing in the UI said so in a way anyone would notice. Its card still showed a name, an address and a full set of settings; the status strip reported "0/1 servers connected" in the same neutral styling as every other number; and step 2 said "No servers available yet", which reads as "you haven't added a server" and sends you off to re-add one you already have. The result was a federated library that had simply stopped working with no visible cause. Now: a banner at the top of the page names every switched-off server and states the consequence, the server's own card is marked with a DISABLED pill and an accent border plus an inline note, the "0/1" turns amber when servers exist but none are live, the checkbox reads "Enabled - sync and play from this server" rather than a bare "Enabled", and step 2 distinguishes "no servers configured" from "all of them are off". Also corrects a genuinely misleading label: the streaming mode picker called Direct "(recommended)" unconditionally and Proxy "slower". Direct hands the player a raw URL to the remote, so nothing retries a dropped read - over the internet, a tunnel or a reverse proxy that is precisely what surfaces as stuttering, while Proxy's resumable relay absorbs it. The two are now labelled "best on a local network" and "best over the internet", each with a line explaining the trade-off.
